lopezmeza_2016.name: Monod growth with Luedeking-Piret mAb formation (CHO, 33 and 37 C)
lopezmeza_2016.description: The model describes growth, glucose use, and infliximab-biosimilar production by native and recombinant CHO-S cells. It combines first-order growth during the exponential phase with a threshold-modified Monod growth relationship, a cell-yield description of glucose consumption, and a Luedeking–Piret description of antibody formation. The authors developed it using batch cultures in shake flasks at different initial glucose concentrations and temperatures, then evaluated its product-formation description in instrumented batch and fed-batch bioreactors. Cell, glucose, lactate, and active antibody concentrations were measured daily. The authors present the simple kinetic models as tools for understanding and characterizing cell-culture processes, and for applications such as monitoring, control, and optimization.

facts.text: The model concerns native CHO-S cells and an in-house engineered recombinant CHO-S clone producing an infliximab biosimilar.
facts.quote: we used a CHO-S clone engineered in-house (Carrillo-Cocom et al. 2014; González-Leal et al. 2011) to produce a biosimilar of the monoclonal antibody infliximab and its native counterpart

facts.text: Cultures used CD Opti CHO medium supplemented with 8 mM glutamine.
facts.quote: The cell culture medium consisted of CD Opti CHO (Invitrogen, Carlsbad, CA, USA) supplemented with 8-mM glutamine (Invitrogen, Carlsbad, CA, USA).

facts.text: Shake-flask batch cultures used 125-mL flasks with a 30-mL working volume.
facts.quote: Batch cultures were performed using naive (n-CHO) or recombinant cells (r-CHO) in 125-mL shake flasks with 30-mL working volume.

facts.text: Shake-flask cultures were inoculated at about 2 × 10⁵ viable cells/mL and incubated at 33 or 37 °C, 125 rpm, and 8% CO₂.
facts.quote: Cultures were seeded at a viable cell density of ~2 × 10⁵ cells/mL and maintained at 33 or 37 °C in an 8 % CO₂ humidified orbital shaking incubator at 125 rpm

facts.text: Shake-flask batch experiments tested initial glucose concentrations of 1.2, 2.4, 3.6, and 4.8 g/L.
facts.quote: Experiments were run at different initial substrate concentrations, ranging from 1.2 to 4.8 g/L of glucose (1.2, 2.4, 3.6, and 4.8 g/L).

facts.text: Shake-flask cultures were run in triplicate with daily sampling and were stopped after 7 days for recombinant cells or 10 days for naive cells.
facts.quote: All batch cultures were performed in triplicate with daily sampling. Cultures were terminated at day 7 for the r-CHO cell line and at day 10 for the n-CHO line

facts.text: Instrumented bioreactor experiments used 1.6-L vessels with a 1.0-L working volume and were conducted only with recombinant cells.
facts.quote: Bioreactor-batch and fed-batch cultures were performed only with the recombinant cell line at basal medium concentration. Experiments were performed in 1.6-L bioreactors (DASGIP, Julich, Germany) with 1.0-L working volume.

facts.text: Bioreactor cultures were agitated at 80 rpm and supplied with 2 standard L/h of gas to maintain dissolved oxygen at 40% saturation.
facts.quote: Cultures were seeded at a viable cell density of ~2 × 10⁵ cells/mL and maintained at 33 °C with an 80-rpm rate of agitation. Cultures were supplied with a gas mixture (2 sL/h) consisting of air, oxygen, nitrogen, and carbon dioxide to maintain a dissolved oxygen saturation of 40 %.

facts.text: The methods describe fed-batch operation with five intermittent additions of feed, each 10% of the initial culture volume, starting on day 1, and a temperature reduction on day 7.
facts.quote: The fed-batch protocol consisted of a temperature reduction (31 °C) on the seventh day and five intermittent feed additions (CD EfficientFeed™ B, Invitrogen, Carlsbad, CA, USA) of 10 % the initial volume starting on day 1.

facts.text: Bioreactor batch runs lasted 10 days and fed-batch runs lasted 20 days, with duplicate cultures and daily sampling.
facts.quote: All cultures were performed by duplicate with daily sampling. Batch cultures were terminated after 10 days and fed-batch cultures after 20 days.

facts.text: The measured time series included viable cell density, glucose, lactic acid, and monoclonal antibody concentrations.
facts.quote: The time evolution of cell, glucose, lactic acid concentration and monoclonal antibody concentrations was monitored on a daily basis

facts.text: Cell density and viability were measured by trypan-blue exclusion using a Guava easyCyte flow cytometer.
Glucose and lactate were measured by HPLC with refractive-index detection using an Aminex HPX 87H column and 5 mM sulfuric acid mobile phase.
The antibody assay quantified active monoclonal antibody in culture samples by ELISA.
facts.quote: An enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) was used to quantify the active monoclonal antibody in the collected samples

facts.text: The authors characterize their approach as simple, unstructured kinetic modeling.
facts.quote: The majority of the kinetic models in the literature are categorized as unstructured

facts.text: The authors treat cell growth as first-order in cell concentration during at least the initial portion of exponential growth.
facts.quote: We observed that cell growth was a first-order process (Eq. 1) with respect to cell concentration, at least at the beginning of the exponential growth phase

facts.text: The growth relationship is Monod-type but includes a nonzero glucose threshold below which growth is not observed.
facts.quote: a useful growth model requires the inclusion of a threshold substrate parameter

facts.text: The fitted Monod parameters for recombinant cells were reported to change little with temperature, whereas those for naive cells changed with temperature.
facts.quote: Interestingly, the Monod-type kinetic values for recombinant cells do not change significantly as a function of temperature

facts.text: The model relates glucose consumption to cell growth through a cell/substrate yield coefficient.
facts.quote: The material balance for substrate consumption was assumed to be represented by Eq. 4.

facts.text: The authors found that the cell/substrate yield coefficient varied with glucose concentration rather than remaining constant.
facts.quote: Our results suggested that the cell/substrate yield coefficient was not constant, but was a function of the substrate concentration

facts.text: Antibody formation is represented with a Luedeking–Piret model, combining growth-associated and viable-cell-associated production.
facts.quote: the rate of product synthesis can be a function of both cellular density ([X]) and the rate of cell growth

facts.text: The authors describe production by this recombinant line as mixed-mode, with formation related to both growth rate and viable-cell concentration.
facts.quote: it followed mixed-mode production kinetics, where at any given time the rate of product formation depends on the rate of cell growth and the current viable cell concentration.

facts.text: Lactate was measured and discussed, but the model laws described in the paper do not include a lactate balance or lactate effect.
Cell and glucose profiles during exponential growth were fitted with second-order polynomials and differentiated to estimate growth and glucose-consumption rates.
facts.quote: The viable cell [X] and glucose concentration [S] profiles observed in the exponential phase of batch experiments were fitted to second-order polynomial equations using Excel Software

facts.text: For antibody-production analysis, viable-cell profiles were fitted with a sixth-order polynomial and differentiated to estimate cell-growth rates.
facts.quote: the viable cell concentration profile [X] was fit to a sixth-order polynomial. The polynomial equation was derived to obtain the experimental cell production rate

facts.text: The growth-kinetic parameters were obtained using Lineweaver–Burk linearization, and a linear regression was accepted only when its r² exceeded 0.97.
facts.quote: A Lineweaver–Burk linearization was used to obtain values for the kinetic parameters

facts.text: The authors selected the product-formation coefficients by fitting multiple cell-density and antibody-production data sets and numerically integrating the model.
facts.quote: The values of α and β were chosen to fit several experimental data sets of cell concentration and mAb production profiles.

facts.text: For 37 °C recombinant batch data, the authors iteratively adjusted selected growth, yield, and production parameters while holding the threshold and one production coefficient fixed.
facts.quote: The parameters [S]t and α were kept constant, while μmax, Yx/s, and β were varied iteratively until a good agreement between the [X], [S], and [P] experimental time series and the simulation values was achieved.

facts.text: The paper does not give a consolidated count of model states, equations, or estimated parameters.
The authors report that the product-formation parameters fitted shake-flask data over initial substrate concentrations from 2.4 to 4.5 g/L.
facts.quote: These α and β values can be used to accurately reproduce data obtained in experiments where the initial substrate concentration ranges from 2.4 to 4.5 g/L

facts.text: The product-formation description was tested on recombinant-cell batch cultures in instrumented bioreactors, and the authors report a good fit using the shake-flask parameter set.
The authors also applied the batch-derived kinetic parameter set to fed-batch cultures, where they report that the model fit the measured data.
facts.quote: The Luedeking–Piret model previously tested for batch processes (in shake flasks and bioreactors) fit the experimental data

facts.text: For fed-batch validation, the paper describes a representative instrumented run with a temperature shift from 37 to 33 °C on day 7.
facts.quote: The culture was set to 37 °C for the first 7 days of culture. At day 7, the temperature set point was decreased to 33 °C.

facts.text: A single pair of product-formation coefficients did not describe all the 37 °C batch data sets, and the authors suggest lactate inhibition as a possible model improvement.
The authors state that the proposed product-formation parameters fit experimental data sets in the range of 31–33 °C.
facts.quote: The proposed parameter values for the Luedeking–Piret model fit reasonably well with several independent experimental data sets in the range of 31–33 °C.

facts.text: The paper places its growth model alongside Monod-like and logistic hybridoma models, Monod and metabolic-flux models, and dynamic metabolic models for nonproducing CHO cells.

The authors contrast their approach with earlier recombinant-cell studies using structured kinetic, logistic, Monte Carlo, and regression models, including Sandadi et al. 2011, Goudar et al. 2009, Xing et al. 2010, and Farges et al. 2008.
facts.quote: structured kinetic (Sandadi et al. 2011) and logistic models for r-CHO producing IgG (Goudar et al. 2009); Monte Carlo methodology model for CHO cells producing B1 fusion proteins (Xing et al. 2010); and logistic and regression models for a CHO cell line producing IFN-γ (Farges et al. 2008).

facts.text: The product-formation model is identified as a Luedeking–Piret model, citing Luedeking and Piret 1959.
facts.quote: A Luedeking–Piret-type model (Luedeking and Piret 1959) was proposed for the modeling of antibody production

facts.text: The authors propose simple kinetic models as practical tools for process characterization, online monitoring, process control, and optimization.
facts.quote: simple models are particularly appreciated; they are easy to use in real process characterization, online monitoring, process control and process optimization scenarios

facts.text: The paper does not report a code or data repository.
